final_answer:
Note on comparability: GE's reported FY2022 revenue varies substantially across filings because of two major divestitures — the January 2023 spin-off of GE HealthCare and the April 2024 spin-off of GE Vernova. The FY2022 10-K reported total revenue of $76,555 million for the whole company as it existed at that time [DOC-1]. After the HealthCare spin-off, GE's FY2023 10-K restated FY2022 revenue (continuing operations, excluding HealthCare) to $58,100 million [DOC-2]. After the subsequent Vernova spin-off, GE Aerospace's FY2024 10-K further restated FY2022 revenue (continuing operations, excluding both HealthCare and Vernova) to $29,139 million [DOC-3], with both businesses' results reclassified as discontinued operations for all periods presented [DOC-4].

Because the question asks about "the company now known as GE Aerospace," the appropriate comparison uses the FY2024 10-K's continuing-operations basis, which excludes both spun-off businesses (HealthCare and Vernova) from both periods, making FY2022 ($29,139 million) and FY2024 ($38,702 million) figures comparable on a like-for-like basis [DOC-3].

Growth calculation:
($38,702M − $29,139M) / $29,139M = $9,563M / $29,139M ≈ 32.8%

ANSWER: Revenue grew approximately 32.8% from FY2022 ($29,139 million, restated for GE Aerospace continuing operations) to FY2024 ($38,702 million), per the comparable figures in GE Aerospace's FY2024 10-K [DOC-3]. Note that this differs greatly from unadjusted comparisons using the originally reported FY2022 figure of $76,555 million [DOC-1], which included the now-divested HealthCare and Vernova businesses and is not comparable to FY2024 GE Aerospace results.

Question: What was the revenue growth from fiscal year 2022 to fiscal year 2024 for the company now known as GE Aerospace?
